findings: Only source384-5cpu-16gib-planner180@1 selects 180 seconds; None and both existing profiles retain 90. Existing resource and execution dictionaries remain unchanged.

The new profile retains the extended profile resource/admission contract: 5 CPUs, 16 GiB memory, 900-second driver, 840-second work cutoff and 60-second cleanup reserve; it does not extend the enclosing trial.

Preparation signs max_latency_ms=180000 in the native planning request and stores planner_timeout_seconds=180. Replay verifies the signed request equality, typed timeout and selected profile limit before planning.

plan() defaults to the replayed limit, accepts only integer explicit timeouts in [1,limit], and replays current prepared state again before provider dispatch. Unsigned metadata or request substitution cannot raise the allowance.

The driver selects min(profile planner limit, remaining work minus 30 seconds); isolated provider invocation and process communication retain additional remaining-work clamps and the outer work alarm.
Native prompt planner uses the smaller configured timeout and signed request latency; provider/router output-token and tool boundaries are unchanged.
Warm recovery still requires the original extended profile exactly; setup-cache resource allowlist remains unchanged and excludes planner180.
